chains.title: C228T creates a de novo ETS site selectively used by the GABP complex (GABPA with GABPB1), activating TERT transcription
chains.cell_type: Glioblastoma tumour cells (also melanoma, bladder urothelium)

links.claim: The G>A change creates a GGAA ETS core: the whole Ets group G003 predicts stronger alt binding (best model ETV5 z 166.19, effect +2.12; site strength ref 97.1th -> alt 99.3th percentile), and GABPA has its own QBiC-SELEX model in that group (z 68.47, 15.52 TPM in glioblastoma lines). The Ets group is one shared specificity, so I choose GABPA within it on two external lines of evidence rather than on the group z-scores: ENCODE ChIP-seq places GABPA peaks directly over this position in two biosamples (E16) while no ETS1 peak contains it (E17), and the literature reports that the GABP tetramer, not other ETS factors, is responsible for activation at TERTp mutations across 53 cell lines and 6 recurrent mutations (E18b, E18c, E18d). GABPB1 coverage was not shown by any screen row and is not claimed here.
The variant lies in an ENCODE promoter-like cCRE (EH38E3622530) with high DNase, H3K4me3 and H3K27ac, i.e. the active TERT core promoter, and VEP annotates a promoter regulatory feature there.

The affected promoter coincides with the TERT TSS (0.0 kb; CLPTM1L is 50 kb away), so TERT is the regulated gene; this rests on proximity plus the promoter annotation, not on eQTL or perturbation data.

TERTp mutations are frequent in IDH-wildtype glioblastoma and in melanoma (50-82% of cases); GABPA is expressed in glioblastoma lines (15.52 TPM) and the GABP mechanism was shown across many cancer types. No cited evidence covers bladder specifically.

Promoter activation by the recruited GABP complex raises TERT expression and reactivates telomerase, which supports continued proliferation; the cited evidence shows the activation mechanism and that low TERT triggers senescence, not a direct allele-specific expression measurement.

predictions: Allele-specific GABPA/GABPB1 ChIP signal at the TERT promoter only on the mutant allele and only in C228T-containing lines
GABPA or GABPB1 knockdown lowers TERT mRNA and telomerase activity selectively in C228T-mutant cells, with little effect in wild-type lines
Reporter gain of the A allele is abolished by destroying the created GGAA core while leaving flanks intact
falsified_if: GABPA/GABPB1 show no allele-specific occupancy at the mutant promoter
GABPA loss does not reduce TERT in C228T-mutant cells, or reduces it equally in wild-type cells
The A allele shows no increase in reporter activity

predictions: Allele-specific reporter and endogenous base-editing experiments show no change in TERT promoter output
No allele-specific TF occupancy at the site
Any association reflects a linked variant (for example the rs2853669 haplotype) or recurrent mutagenesis at a hotspot

Allele-specific ChIP identifies a factor bound only on the mutant allele

chains.title: The created ETS site is used by another abundant ETS factor (ETS1 or ELF1) rather than GABP

links.claim: Group G003 predicts stronger alt binding for 18 ETS models; ETS1 has its own model and the highest expression in glioblastoma lines (61.0 TPM), so on expression alone it could occupy the created GGAA. Against this, no ENCODE ETS1 peak contains the site (absence may reflect missing experiments), and multiple ETS factors bind the -124C>T sequence in vitro without necessarily driving activation.
The created site lies inside the active TERT promoter-like cCRE with strong DNase/H3K4me3/H3K27ac signal.
TERT is the gene whose TSS coincides with this promoter.
ETS1 is abundant in glioblastoma lines (61 TPM); abundance is not occupancy, and no ChIP evidence supports binding here.
If ETS1 occupied the new site it would activate TERT and sustain telomerase; no cited ETS1 perturbation or reporter data support this step.

predictions: ETS1 (or ELF1) ChIP, not GABPA, shows mutant-allele-specific binding at the TERT promoter
ETS1 knockdown reduces TERT selectively in mutant lines while GABPA knockdown does not
Allelic effect size tracks ETS1 expression across tumour lines
falsified_if: GABPA/GABPB1 but not ETS1/ELF1 occupy the mutant site
ETS1 depletion leaves TERT unchanged in C228T-mutant cells

chains.title: The mutation reduces ZNF148 binding at the wild-type promoter, relieving repression of TERT

links.claim: ZNF148 was identified as a wild-type TERT promoter binder with reduced interaction with the -124C>T (C228T) allele, so the reference allele binds it more. ZNF148 does not appear in any screen row shown and has not been looked up, so its QBiC-SELEX coverage is not_checked and no QBiC direction is claimed for it.
The site is within the active TERT promoter cCRE.
TERT is the gene at this promoter (TSS 0.0 kb).
No cited evidence gives ZNF148 expression or occupancy in glioblastoma lines; the cell-type step is unsupported.
If ZNF148 restrains the wild-type promoter, its reduced binding would de-repress TERT; the cited work shows reduced interaction only, not a repressor function or an expression change.

predictions: ZNF148 ChIP shows reference-allele-specific binding at the TERT promoter
ZNF148 knockdown raises TERT from the reference promoter but not from the mutant promoter
Reporter gain of the A allele survives destruction of the created GGAA core, because the driver is loss of ZNF148 rather than ETS gain
falsified_if: ZNF148 shows no allele-specific binding at this site
ZNF148 depletion does not change TERT output from the reference promoter
Reporter gain requires an intact GGAA core

chains.title: The mutation destroys an AP-2 (TFAP2A) site, relieving repression of TERT

links.claim: AP-2 group G030 predicts weaker alt binding (best model TFAP2E z -36.84, effect -1.289; ref 99.5th -> alt 96.5th percentile); within the group TFAP2A has its own model, the highest expression in glioblastoma lines (9.65 TPM) and z -28.06, so it is the plausible lost factor. This is an in vitro prediction only.
The predicted lost site lies in the active TERT promoter cCRE; no evidence shows an AP-2 site is functional there.
TERT is the promoter's own gene.
TFAP2A is expressed in glioblastoma lines (9.65 TPM); no cited evidence supports an AP-2 role in melanoma TERT regulation.
If AP-2 repressed this promoter, its loss would raise TERT; no cited evidence supports a repressor role for AP-2 here, and this chain does not explain the created GGAA.

predictions: TFAP2A ChIP signal at the TERT promoter is reduced on the mutant allele
TFAP2A overexpression lowers output from the reference but not the mutant promoter
Mutating only the AP-2 half-site, without creating GGAA, raises promoter activity
falsified_if: No AP-2 occupancy at the TERT promoter in these cell types
TFAP2A perturbation does not alter TERT promoter activity
Reporter gain requires an intact GGAA core

grades_v0.reason: E06 shows GABPA has its own model, alt binds more (z 68.47, 15.52 TPM), but this is a binding prediction only. The choice of GABPA over ETV5/ELF1/ETS1 rests on outside knowledge (GABPA/GABPB1 multimer recruitment), not on any cited evidence. No ChIP or perturbation is cited. GABPB1 is not in the evidence.
E03 places the variant in PLS cCRE EH38E3622530 with high DNase, H3K27ac and H3K4me3, and E01 gives a promoter regulatory feature. This supports an active promoter element.

E02 puts TERT at 0.0 kb from the TSS, and E01 gives a TERT upstream consequence. There is no eQTL or perturbation evidence, but proximity at a promoter is strong. The claim that it is not CLPTM1L is only distance-based.

E04a supports TERT promoter mutations in melanoma, and E04f supports frequent mutation in IDH-wt GBM. Nothing cited covers bladder, and 'dominant mechanism' over-claims. No cell-type-specific expression or binding evidence for the mutant site is given, only DepMap TPM for GABPA.

E04a links TERT promoter mutations to telomerase activation in melanoma. E04e only shows that USP10/FOXM1 loss lowers TERT and triggers senescence, which does not show that C228T increases TERT expression or prevents senescence. No allele-specific expression or reporter data are cited.

ETS1 has its own model with alt binding more (E06, 61 TPM), but the pick is by expression alone. ETS1 is named only in the TF coverage list, with no z-score or effect shown. ELF1 is cited as an alternative but not graded. Prediction only.
E03 shows the active PLS cCRE overlapping the variant.
E02 and E03 place the variant at the TERT TSS/promoter.
E06 gives only ETS1 expression in glioblastoma lines (61 TPM). Expression does not show occupancy at the site. The claim is inferred from RNA abundance.
E04a and E04f concern TERT promoter mutation frequency, not ETS1-driven activation. No ETS1 perturbation, ChIP or reporter data are cited.

E09 shows AP-2 group alt binds less, and TFAP2A has its own model (9.65 TPM). The best model is TFAP2E at 0.49 TPM, and the TFAP2A z-score is -28.06. The effect is a prediction only. The direction agrees with a loss, but the repressor role is assumed.
E03 gives an active promoter cCRE at the variant. It does not show that the AP-2 site is functional there.
E02 and E03 give TERT at the TSS.
E09 shows TFAP2A expression in GBM lines, but the melanoma lineage-factor claim is not backed by any cited evidence.

E04a does not mention AP-2 or repression. The loss-of-repression claim has no support. The direction also conflicts with the known gain of reporter activity requiring a GGAA core, which is not tested here.

E11 shows alt binds less for ZIC4/ZIC1, and ZIC1 has its own model (13.23 TPM). ZIC1 is only a pick by expression. The title also mentions ZNF/ELF3 gain, which is not tied to the ZIC1 chain. This is a prediction only.
E03 shows an active promoter cCRE overlapping the variant.
E02 and E03 place TERT at the promoter.
E11 gives glioblastoma ZIC1 TPM only. The claim that ZIC1 is not expressed in melanoma or bladder is not shown by any evidence.
E04f contains nothing on ZIC1 or repression. It also notes a pan-cancer pattern, which the chain admits conflicts with its own glioma-restricted prediction.

grades_final.reason: Literature quotes E18b-d show the GABP tetramer is responsible for TERTp mutation activation across 53 lines (perturbation-level). E16 gives GABPA ChIP peaks over the site, E05/E06 show an own GABPA model with alt binding more, and E17 shows no ETS1 peak. GABPB1 is explicitly not claimed. The choice of GABPA is justified by external evidence. Caveat: E18b-d speak to TERTp mutations generally, and C228T is not named in the quotes, but E18c says the two most common mutations recruit GABP.

E03 places the variant in PLS cCRE EH38E3622530 with high DNase, H3K27ac and H3K4me3 z-scores, and E01 gives a promoter regulatory feature. These are maxima across biosamples, so glioblastoma specificity is not shown, but the element call is sound for a core promoter.

Support rests on proximity (TSS 0.0 kb) and promoter annotation (E01-E03). The chain itself admits there is no eQTL or perturbation data, and E18b's promoter activation is only indirect. Consistent but indirect.

E04a and E04f show frequent TERTp mutations in melanoma and IDH-wildtype GBM, and E06 shows GABPA at 15.52 TPM in GBM lines. E18b shows the mechanism across many lines. Bladder is correctly flagged as uncovered, and GBM-specific perturbation data are not quoted. Context only.

E18b supports promoter activation by GABP, and E04e shows that loss of USP10/FOXM1 lowers TERT and triggers senescence (indirect, not specific to this variant). E18f is a review. No direct allele-specific expression or telomerase measurement is cited, as the chain admits. The direction is consistent.

G003 predicts alt binding more and ETS1 has its own model at 61 TPM, but this is prediction plus expression only. E17 shows no ETS1 peak (possibly missing experiments), and E18e shows only in vitro binding of multiple ETS factors. E18b-d point to GABP instead. Nothing shows ETS1 acts here.
E03 shows the variant lies in the active promoter-like cCRE with strong DNase, H3K4me3 and H3K27ac. The element is the same as for H1, but this link does not depend on which TF binds.
The TERT TSS coincides with the promoter (E02, E03), so the link is by proximity and annotation only, with no perturbation or QTL evidence.
E06 gives ETS1 expression of 61 TPM in GBM lines, but abundance is not occupancy, and E17 does not support binding at the site. Expression context only.
No evidence is cited, and the chain admits no ETS1 perturbation or reporter data. E18b indicates GABP, not ETS1, is responsible.

E18e shows ZNF148 binds the wild-type TERT promoter, with reduced interaction with -124C>T (C228T), so the ref-binds-more direction is consistent. This is literature-level and in vitro, and the quote does not specify the assay or glioblastoma. The qbic_coverage of not_checked is honestly stated, and a qbic_tf_detail lookup of ZNF148 should be run.
E03 shows the variant lies in the active TERT promoter cCRE. The element is correct, though the chain does not show that ZNF148 binds within it.
Proximity to the TERT TSS and promoter annotation (E02, E03) are the only evidence, with no perturbation or QTL data.
The chain itself cites no evidence of ZNF148 expression or occupancy in glioblastoma lines.

E18e shows only reduced ZNF148 interaction with the mutant allele. Moreover, E18e describes ZNF148 as an activator of the wild-type promoter (E18 hit title: transcriptional activators), which contradicts the repressor and de-repression claim. Direction is not supported, and the chain cites no repressor function or expression change.

E05/E09 show the AP-2 group G030 predicts weaker alt binding, and TFAP2A has its own model (z -28.06, 9.65 TPM). The choice of TFAP2A within the group rests on expression only. It is an in vitro prediction without ChIP or perturbation support, and the direction is internally consistent.
E03 shows the variant is in an active promoter cCRE, but no evidence shows an AP-2 site is functional there, as the chain admits.
The TERT TSS coincides with the promoter (E02, E03), so the link is by proximity only. There is no AP-2 data tying the site to TERT regulation.
E09 gives TFAP2A expression of 9.65 TPM in GBM lines, which is expression context only. The melanoma claim is acknowledged as unsupported, and no occupancy data are cited.
No evidence is cited for an AP-2 repressor role at TERT, and the chain admits it does not explain the created GGAA site.

PMID 42859331 (2026): CDKN2A deletion associated with poor prognosis in patients with TERT promoter wild-type, IDH wild-type glioblastoma.

A major molecular feature of melanoma is abnormal telomerase activation; this is most often caused by telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT) promoter mutations, which occur in 50-82% of cases and are the most common noncoding alteration in this cancer.
CDKN2A and CDK4 mutations act through UV-dependent and cell cycle disruption pathways, while BAP1, POT1, and TERT mutations are considered UV-independent.
The single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) rs2853669, also located in the TERT promoter, may influence telomerase activity, though its clinical relevance in GBM remains unclear.

Patients carrying the SNP and TPM on the same allele (C/C and T/C cis) had shorter overall survival than those carrying them on different alleles (T/T or T/C trans; 19 vs 25 months, p = 0.048), and TERT expression was also lower in this group (p = 0.038).
Additionally, loss of either USP10 or FOXM1 suppresses the expression of the downstream target Telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT), triggering cellular senescence.

TERT promoter (TERTp) mutations are among the most frequent molecular alterations in isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH) wild-type glioblastoma (GBM), yet the molecular profiles and prognostic implications associated with TERTp status remain incompletely characterized.

TERT promoter (TERTp) mutations create a de novo E26 transformation-specific (ETS) transcription factor binding motif.
Here, we analyzed 53 cell lines representing 16 cancer types and 6 recurrent TERTp mutations and found that the GA-binding protein (GABP) tetramer is responsible for promoter activation in all cases.
Beyond the two most common point mutations, which selectively recruit the ETS factor GABP to activate TERT, the significance of other variants is unknown.

The duplications recruit a GABP tetramer by virtue of the native ETS motif and its precisely spaced duplicated counterpart, activate the promoter and are clonal in a TERT expressing multifocal glioblastoma.

Although we confirmed binding of multiple ETS factors to the mutant -146C > T and -124C > T sequences, we identified E4F1 as a -57A > C-specific binder and ZNF148 as a TERT wild-type (WT) promoter binder that showed reduced interaction with the -124C > T allele.

These mutations promote TERT gene expression by multiple mechanisms, including the generation of novel binding sites for nuclear transcription factors, displacement of negative regulators from DNA G-quadruplexes, recruitment of epigenetic activators and disruption of long-range interactions between TERT locus and telomeres.
Specifically, AURKB, via REST, is recruited to TERTp MUT by TRIM28.
